source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: What problem is Google DeepMind's Levels of AGI (artificial general intelligence) framework, mentioned in the lecture, designed to address?

options.text: It provides a single yes-or-no test any model can be run through once.
options.feedback: This is the opposite of the framework's purpose. A single pass/fail threshold is precisely the thing it was built to replace, because that threshold kept being redrawn.

options.text: It replaces a single yes/no threshold with graded levels of performance and generality.
options.feedback: Grading performance and generality against what a model actually does gives you something checkable, instead of one label that gets redefined every time it is met.

options.text: It certifies which company may use the term AGI in its marketing.
options.feedback: The notes describe no certification or naming-rights function. The framework is a way of measuring capability, not of policing who may use a word.

options.text: It counts a model's parameters to decide whether it qualifies as general.
options.feedback: Parameter count is not what the framework grades. It looks at levels of performance and generality in a model's actual behavior.
